title: Beak depth in Daphne Major finches tracked seed hardness after 2004 drought
body:
Re-analysed the long-term Geospiza fortis dataset for 1998–2010.
[Step] Phenotyping
  [Input] caliper beak measurements, n = 312 individuals/year, [Tool] dial caliper, ±0.1 mm
[Step] Seed survey
  [Tool] quadrat survey, [Output] hard-seed fraction rose from 0.18 to 0.61 after 2004
[Step] Trend
  [Output] mean beak depth shifted +0.43 mm by 2007 (p < 0.01)
The direction of selection matches the shift in seed hardness, supporting the established interpretation that drought-driven food composition is the proximate cause. Within-generation phenotypic plasticity cannot be ruled out without offspring-of-survivor data.
